purpose: Independent practice of C1.1 — describing a repeating pattern, predicting the next element, and creating an original repeating pattern. Used as Lesson 1 consolidation and as evidence for the diagnostic checklist.
student_learning_goal: I can describe a repeating pattern and predict what comes next.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can describe a repeating pattern and predict what comes next.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner of the header, smiling and holding the conductor's baton. Small (~1.5in tall). References the shared 'Coco the Conductor' asset from blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Bea and Finn are leading the parade. Look at the pattern. Draw or sticker the animal that comes next. Then circle the word that finishes the sentence below.
parts.visual_layout: Horizontal parade strip centred at the top, 5 cells wide, each cell ~1.2in square. Cells 1–4 are filled with the animal icons in the order Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn. Cell 5 has a dashed outline (no fill) to signal the empty space the student fills in. Footprints decorate the strip beneath the cells. To the left of the strip, a small reference key shows just the Bea and Finn icons with their names underneath. Below the strip, a Grade 1 sentence frame: 'I predict ____ comes next because the pattern repeats.' with the word options 'Bea / Finn / Bibi / Moss' shown beneath as bubbles to circle.

parts.answer_key: Cell 7 = Bea. Cell 8 = Finn. Wait — re-check: the rule is ABC (Bea-Finn-Bibi). After Bibi, the rule restarts with Bea. So cell 7 = Bea, cell 8 = Finn. Full sequence: Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn.

parts.answer_key: Any valid repeating pattern using two OR three of the four animals across 6 cells. Examples of valid responses: AB rule (Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn), ABC rule (Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn-Bibi), ABB rule (Bea-Finn-Finn-Bea-Finn-Finn), AAB rule (Bea-Bea-Finn-Bea-Bea-Finn). A response is correct if the pattern repeats consistently across all 6 cells.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and build another parade with three different animals! Can you make an ABC pattern that uses Bea, Bibi, and Moss?
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation artifact. Hand it out at the end of the Action phase. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 with minimal support. For Part 3, look for: (a) the child uses 2 or 3 different animals, (b) the pattern repeats consistently. Use Part 3 as evidence for the diagnostic checklist columns 'Creates 2-element pattern (independent)' and 'Creates 3-element pattern (independent)'. Children who struggle with Part 3 likely need a small-group re-loop on Lesson 1's predicting work before Lesson 2 (rule-naming) requires more abstraction.
